tests.name: Conduct Search Engine Reconnaissance for Information Leakage
objectives: Identify what sensitive design and configuration information of the application, system, or organization is exposed directly (on the organization's site) or indirectly (via third-party services).

tests.name: Fingerprint Web Server
objectives: Determine the version and type of a running web server to enable further discovery of any known vulnerabilities.

tests.name: Review Webserver Metafiles for Information Leakage
objectives: Identify hidden or obfuscated paths and functionality through the analysis of metadata files.
Extract and map other information that could lead to a better understanding of the systems at hand.

tests.name: Attack Surface Identification
objectives: Enumerate all web applications within scope.
Identify DNS names, domains, and virtual hosts associated with the target.
Discover additional domains and subdomains using passive and active DNS techniques.
Analyze digital certificates and Certificate Transparency logs for additional hostnames.

tests.name: Review Web Page Content for Information Leakage
objectives: Review web page comments, metadata, and redirect bodies to find any information leakage.
Gather JavaScript files and review the JS code to better understand the application and to find any information leakage.
Identify if source map files or other frontend debug files exist.

tests.name: Identify Application Entry Points
objectives: Identify possible entry and injection points through request and response analysis.

tests.name: Map Execution Paths Through Application
objectives: Map the target application and understand the principal workflows.

tests.name: Fingerprint Web Application Framework
objectives: Fingerprint the components used by the web applications.
Identify the versions of those components and determine whether any are outdated, unsupported, or affected by known vulnerabilities.

tests.name: Map Application Architecture
objectives: Understand the architecture of the application and the technologies in use.

tests.name: Network Infrastructure Configuration
objectives: Review the applications' configurations set across the network and validate that they are not vulnerable.
Validate that used frameworks and systems are secure and not susceptible to known vulnerabilities due to unmaintained software or default settings and credentials.

Where the infrastructure is cloud-hosted or containerized, review network isolation controls (security groups/NSGs, VPC/subnet layout, load balancer/CDN configuration, service mesh policies, Kubernetes `NetworkPolicy`) for unintended exposure or overly permissive rules.

tests.name: Application Platform Configuration
objectives: Ensure that default, sample, and known files have been removed from the deployed platform, container image, or serverless package.
Validate that no debugging code, debug endpoints, debug modes, or unused modules/dependencies are left enabled in production environments.
Review the logging mechanisms set in place for the application, including what sensitive data may be captured and who/what can access or retain it.
Confirm framework-, container-, and serverless-specific production hardening settings are applied rather than left at insecure defaults.

tests.name: Review Old Backup and Unreferenced Files for Sensitive Information
objectives: Find and analyze old, backup, and unreferenced files - including files exposed only through their extension, and objects left in cloud storage - that might contain sensitive information.
Validate that no system or framework bypasses exist for any rules put in place to prevent these files from being served.

tests.name: Enumerate Infrastructure and Application Admin Interfaces
objectives: Identify hidden administrator interfaces and functionality, including cloud, container-orchestration, API-management, and CI/CD management consoles.
Check any discovered interface for default, weak, or reused credentials, and for exposure to networks/users beyond those intended.

tests.name: HTTP Methods
objectives: Enumerate supported HTTP methods.
Test for access control bypass.
Test HTTP method overriding techniques.

tests.name: HTTP Strict Transport Security
objectives: Review the HSTS header, its directives, and their values for consistency with current best practice.
Confirm the site is protected against the first-request trust gap, either via preload or an otherwise hardened HTTP-to-HTTPS path.
Confirm HSTS is applied consistently across the domain and relevant subdomains, and does not mask mixed-content issues.

tests.name: File Permissions
objectives: Review and identify any rogue file permissions on the host filesystem, in container images/filesystems, and on cloud storage objects.
Assess whether Kubernetes volume mounts and `securityContext` settings enforce least-privilege access to files and secrets.
Identify secrets stored with overly broad permissions, wherever they are held (filesystem, container image, orchestration secret store, cloud secrets manager export, CI artifacts).

tests.name: Subdomain Takeover
objectives: Enumerate all possible domains (previous and current), including wildcard-covered names.
Identify any forgotten or misconfigured domains, and any dangling-service signature not covered by a known response fingerprint.
Identify links and resources that point to external domains, buckets, or accounts that no longer exist and could be claimed.
Where a takeover is confirmed feasible, assess whether the parent application's cookies, CORS policy, OAuth redirect validation, or CSP allowlist extend trust to the claimed subdomain.

tests.name: Cloud Storage
objectives: Assess that the access control configuration for the storage services (bucket/container-level public access, and object/principal-level ACLs or IAM policies) is properly in place.
Assess whether signed/presigned URLs are scoped, time-limited, and handled appropriately.
Assess whether object versioning and lifecycle configuration could expose old or supposedly-removed sensitive data.

tests.name: Content Security Policy
objectives: Review the Content-Security-Policy header or meta element to identify misconfigurations.

tests.name: Path Confusion
objectives: Make sure application paths are configured and normalized consistently across all components (application, proxy, cache, CDN, WAF) that make decisions based on the path.
Identify cases where trailing slashes, case sensitivity, or encoding differences cause a security control (auth/access rules, routing, cache keying) to be bypassed or behave inconsistently.

tests.name: Additional Browser Security Controls
objectives: Identify improperly configured security headers.
Assess the impact of misconfigured security headers.
Validate the correct implementation of required security headers.
Identify third-party scripts and style sheets and determine whether they are pinned with Subresource Integrity.

tests.name: Feature Flag Security Bypass
objectives: Identify feature flags and kill-switches that control security-relevant functionality.
Determine whether feature flag states can be manipulated by an unauthorized client, and verify that backend security controls remain enforced independently of client-side flag state.

Verify that security controls remain consistently enforced across flag transitions, rollbacks, staged deployments, and services or instances, including whether stale security assertions or session state can be reused after a transition.
Evaluate fail-safe behavior when the feature flag service is unavailable.
Identify sensitive information exposed through feature flag configurations, and stale flags that may expose deprecated or unpatched code paths.

tests.name: Web Cache Poisoning
objectives: Identify which responses are cacheable and which request inputs form the cache key.
Find unkeyed headers, cookies, query parameters, or method-override inputs that change the origin response.
Confirm that a clean request without the unkeyed input receives the poisoned or incorrect cached response.
Verify that authenticated or personalized responses are not stored under keys reachable by other users.

tests.name: Role Definitions
objectives: Identify and document roles used by the application.
Attempt to switch, change, or access another role.
Review the granularity of the roles and the needs behind the permissions given.

tests.name: User Registration Process
objectives: Verify that the identity requirements for user registration are aligned with business and security requirements.
Validate the registration process.

tests.name: Account Provisioning Process
objectives: Verify which accounts may provision other accounts and of what type.

tests.name: Account Enumeration and Guessable User Account
objectives: Review processes that pertain to user identification (*e.g.* registration, login, etc.).
Enumerate users where possible through response analysis.
Determine whether look-alike or differently normalized identifiers can impersonate, duplicate or take over an existing account.

tests.name: Email Address Verification
objectives: Determine what an account can do before its email address is verified.
Assess whether verification and email change flows bind the proof of ownership to the right address and account.
Determine whether an attacker can pre-create or keep access to an account that will belong to the victim.
Identify email address syntax that is read differently by the application and by the mail infrastructure, and whether it grants domain-based access.

tests.name: Default Credentials
objectives: Determine whether the application has any user accounts with default passwords.
Review whether new user accounts are created with weak or predictable passwords.

tests.name: Weak Lock Out Mechanism
objectives: Evaluate the account lockout mechanism's ability to mitigate brute force password guessing.
Evaluate the unlock mechanism's resistance to unauthorized account unlocking.

tests.name: Bypassing Authentication Schema
objectives: Ensure that authentication is applied across all services that require it.

tests.name: Vulnerable Remember Password
objectives: Validate that the generated session is managed securely and do not put the user's credentials in danger.

tests.name: Browser Cache Weaknesses
objectives: Review if the application stores sensitive information on the client-side.
Review if access can occur without authorization.

tests.name: Weak Authentication Methods
objectives: Determine the resistance of the application against brute force password guessing using available password dictionaries by evaluating the length, complexity, reuse, and aging requirements of passwords.

tests.name: Weak Security Question Answer
objectives: Determine the complexity and how straight-forward the questions are.
Assess possible user answers and brute force capabilities.

tests.name: Weak Password Change or Reset Functionalities
objectives: Determine whether the password change and reset functionality allows accounts to be compromised.

tests.name: Weaker Authentication in Alternative Channel
objectives: Identify alternative authentication channels.
Assess the security measures used and if any bypasses exists on the alternative channels.

tests.name: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)
objectives: Identify the type of MFA used by the application.
Determine whether the MFA implementation is robust and secure.
Attempt to bypass the MFA.

tests.name: SAML Authentication
objectives: Identify the SAML flow in use and the endpoints involved.
Determine whether the SP validates the signature, and that the signature covers the data the SP uses.
Determine whether the SP enforces the conditions in the assertion (audience, validity period, recipient, and request binding).
Assess whether assertions can be replayed or accepted from an untrusted source.

tests.name: Passkeys and WebAuthn
objectives: Determine whether the RP verifies the challenge, origin and RP ID on registration and authentication.
Assess whether recovery and fallback paths weaken the protection that passkeys provide.
Determine whether adding, listing and removing credentials is protected.
Assess how the RP handles user identification and the data it stores for credentials.

tests.name: OpenID Connect Relying Party
objectives: Confirm the RP validates issuer discovery and authentication claims before creating a session.
Confirm account identity is bound to `(iss, sub)`, not to email alone.
Confirm account-linking and recovery flows cannot attach an attacker-controlled identity to another user's account.
Confirm mix-up defenses when the RP can use more than one OP.
Confirm the RP enforces requested authentication strength claims when it asks for MFA or recent authentication.

tests.name: Directory Traversal and File Include
objectives: Identify injection points that pertain to path traversal.
Assess bypassing techniques and identify the extent of path traversal.

tests.name: Bypassing Authorization Schema
objectives: Assess if unauthenticated, horizontal, or vertical access is possible.

tests.name: Privilege Escalation
objectives: Identify injection points related to privilege manipulation.
Fuzz or otherwise attempt to bypass security measures.

tests.name: Insecure Direct Object References
objectives: Identify points where object references may occur.
Assess the access control measures and if they're vulnerable to IDOR.

tests.name: OAuth Weaknesses
objectives: Determine if OAuth2 implementation is vulnerable or using a deprecated or custom implementation.

tests.name: Session Management Schema
objectives: Gather session tokens, for the same user and for different users where possible.
Analyze and ensure that enough randomness exists to stop session forging attacks.
Modify cookies that are not signed and contain information that can be manipulated.

tests.name: Cookies Attributes
objectives: Ensure that the proper security configuration is set for cookies.

tests.name: Session Fixation
objectives: Analyze the authentication mechanism and its flow.
Force cookies and assess the impact.

tests.name: Exposed Session Variables
objectives: Ensure that proper encryption is implemented.
Review the caching configuration.
Assess the channel and methods' security.

tests.name: Cross Site Request Forgery
objectives: Determine whether it is possible to initiate requests on a user's behalf that are not initiated by the user.

tests.name: Logout Functionality
objectives: Assess the logout UI.
Verify that the session is properly terminated server-side after logout.

tests.name: Session Timeout
objectives: Validate that an idle timeout exists and is enforced server-side.
Validate that an absolute timeout limits the total lifetime of a session.

tests.name: Session Puzzling
objectives: Identify all session variables.
Break the logical flow of session generation.

tests.name: Session Hijacking
objectives: Identify vulnerable session cookies.
Hijack vulnerable cookies and assess the risk level.

tests.name: JSON Web Tokens
objectives: Determine whether the JWTs expose sensitive information.
Determine whether the JWTs can be tampered with or modified.

tests.name: Concurrent Sessions
objectives: Evaluate the application's session management by assessing the handling of multiple active sessions for a single user account.

tests.name: Reflected Cross Site Scripting
objectives: Identify variables that are reflected in responses.
Assess the input they accept and the encoding that gets applied on return (if any).

tests.name: Stored Cross Site Scripting
objectives: Identify stored input that is reflected on the client-side.
Assess the input they accept and the encoding that gets applied on return (if any).

tests.name: HTTP Parameter Pollution
objectives: Identify the back end and the parsing method used.
Assess injection points and try bypassing input filters using HPP.

tests.name: SQL Injection
objectives: Identify SQL injection points.
Assess the severity of the injection and the level of access that can be achieved through it.

tests.name: LDAP Injection
objectives: Identify LDAP injection points.
Assess the severity of the injection.

tests.name: XML Injection
objectives: Identify XML injection points.
Assess the types of exploits that can be attained and their severities.

tests.name: SSI Injection
objectives: Identify SSI injection points.
Assess the severity of the injection.

tests.name: XPath Injection
objectives: Identify XPATH injection points.

tests.name: IMAP SMTP Injection
objectives: Identify IMAP/SMTP injection points.
Understand the data flow and deployment structure of the system.
Assess the injection impacts.

tests.name: Code Injection
objectives: Identify injection points where you can inject code into the application.
Assess the injection severity.

tests.name: Command Injection
objectives: Identify and assess command injection points.
Bypass special characters and OS commands filter.

tests.name: Format String Injection
objectives: Assess whether injecting format string conversion specifiers into user-controlled fields causes undesired behavior from the application.

tests.name: Incubated Vulnerability
objectives: Identify injections that are stored and require a recall step to the stored injection.
Understand how a recall step could occur.
Set listeners or activate the recall step if possible.

tests.name: HTTP Response Splitting
objectives: Identify user-controlled input that is reflected into HTTP response headers.
Assess whether CR (`\r`) and LF (`\n`) characters can be injected into response headers.
Determine the potential impact of successful HTTP Response Splitting attacks, such as cache poisoning or client-side exploitation.

tests.name: HTTP Request Smuggling
objectives: Identify request boundary inconsistencies between frontend and backend components
Detect classic CL/TE desynchronization vulnerabilities
Evaluate protocol translation logic (HTTP/2 → HTTP/1.1)
Assess H2C upgrade handling and downgrade safety
Identify endpoints that ignore the request body (CL.0) and whether a browser can be made to desynchronize its own connection
Confirm backend request queue poisoning

tests.name: Host Header Injection
objectives: Assess if the Host header is being parsed dynamically in the application.
Bypass security controls that rely on the header.

tests.name: Server-side Template Injection
objectives: Detect template injection vulnerability points.
Identify the templating engine.
Build the exploit.

tests.name: Server-Side Request Forgery
objectives: Identify SSRF injection points.
Test if the injection points are exploitable.
Asses the severity of the vulnerability.

tests.name: Mass Assignment
objectives: Identify requests that modify objects
Assess if it is possible to modify fields never intended to be modified from outside

tests.name: CSV Injection
objectives: Identify CSV/spreadsheet export features that include untrusted input.
Verify whether attacker-controlled values are interpreted as formulas when the export is opened in common spreadsheet applications.
Check whether separator/quote injection can move a dangerous prefix to the start of a cell.
Validate whether mitigations remain effective in Microsoft Excel after saving and re-opening the CSV.
Assess practical impact based on who opens the export and how it is used.

tests.name: Prototype Pollution
objectives: Identify functions and libraries that recursively merge, clone, or assign user-controlled properties.
Determine whether user input can reach and modify `Object.prototype`.
Identify gadgets that turn prototype pollution into a concrete impact.

tests.name: Insecure Deserialization
objectives: Identify entry points where the application accepts serialized objects from untrusted
urces (for example, HTTP headers, parameters, or cookies).
Determine the serialization format used by the application.
Assess whether serialized input is validated or restricted prior to deserialization.
Evaluate whether manipulation of serialized data leads to unsafe behavior or security
pact.

tests.name: Server-side URL Redirect
objectives: Identify request parameters, path segments and headers that control a redirect or forward.
Assess whether the validation of redirect targets can be bypassed to reach an external site.
Assess whether a redirect can be used to run script, or chained with OAuth, SSO or SSRF.

tests.name: Unicode Normalization and Case Mapping
objectives: Identify where the application normalizes or changes the case of input.
Determine whether validation, filtering or length checks run before that transformation.
Assess whether the transformation can be used to bypass filters for injection, path traversal or length limits.

tests.name: JSON Parser Differentials
objectives: Identify places where the same JSON document is parsed by more than one component.
Determine whether those components disagree on duplicate keys, key matching, invalid characters, non-standard syntax, numbers or trailing data.
Assess whether a disagreement lets a request pass a check with one value and be processed with another.

tests.name: Server-side Document Rendering Injection
objectives: Identify features that render user-controlled content into documents or images on the server.
Identify the rendering engine and determine whether it processes HTML, CSS, JavaScript, external resources or style sheets supplied by the user.
Assess whether the renderer can be used to read local files, reach internal services or run code.

tests.name: Regular Expression Denial of Service
objectives: Identify inputs that are validated or processed with regular expressions.
Determine whether any of those regular expressions take super-linear time on crafted input.
Determine whether users can supply their own regular expressions and whether those are run with any limits.

tests.name: Improper Error Handling
objectives: Identify existing error output.
Analyze the different output returned.
Determine whether errors expose sensitive information or cause the application to fail open.

tests.name: Weak Transport Layer Security
objectives: Validate the service configuration.
Review the digital certificate's cryptographic strength and validity.
Ensure that the TLS security is not bypassable and is properly implemented across the application.

tests.name: Padding Oracle
objectives: Identify encrypted messages that rely on padding.
Attempt to break the padding of the encrypted messages and analyze the returned error messages for further analysis.

tests.name: Sensitive Information Sent via Unencrypted Channels
objectives: Identify sensitive information transmitted through the various channels.
Assess the privacy and security of the channels used.

tests.name: Weak Cryptographic Primitives
objectives: Provide a guideline for the identification weak encryption or hashing uses and implementations.
Identify weak digital signature algorithms and missing or incorrect signature verification.

tests.name: Business Logic Data Validation
objectives: Identify data injection points.
Validate that all checks are occurring on the backend and can't be bypassed.
Attempt to break the format of the expected data and analyze how the application is handling it.
Determine whether parameters that the frontend restricts (type, range, set of allowed values, or relationship to other fields) are restricted again on the server.

tests.name: Ability to Forge Requests
objectives: Review the project documentation looking for guessable, predictable, or hidden functionality of fields.
Insert logically valid data in order to bypass normal business logic workflow.

tests.name: Integrity Checks
objectives: Review the project documentation for components of the system that move, store, or handle data.
Determine what type of data is logically acceptable by the component and what types the system should guard against.
Determine who should be allowed to modify or read that data in each component.
Attempt to insert, update, or delete data values used by each component that should not be allowed per the business logic workflow.

tests.name: Process Timing
objectives: Review the project documentation for system functionality that may be impacted by time.
Develop and execute misuse cases.

tests.name: Number of Times a Function Can Be Used Limits
objectives: Identify functions that must set limits to the times they can be called.
Assess if there is a logical limit set on the functions and if it is properly validated.

tests.name: Circumvention of Work Flows
objectives: Review the project documentation for methods to skip or go through steps in the application process in a different order from the intended business logic flow.
Develop a misuse case and try to circumvent every logic flow identified.

tests.name: Defenses Against Application Misuse
objectives: Generate notes from all tests conducted against the system.
Review which tests had a different functionality based on aggressive input.
Understand the defenses in place and verify if they are enough to protect the system against bypassing techniques.

tests.name: Upload of Unexpected File Types
objectives: Verify that temporary file references remain bound to the uploading user, original field, and validated file type.
Determine whether expired or missing upload metadata causes the application to reject the reference or safely revalidate the underlying file.
Check whether references can be reused in fields with different validation requirements or by users who do not own the files.
Verify that file delivery does not allow untrusted content to execute under the application's origin.
Review the project documentation for file types that are rejected by the system.
Verify that the unwelcomed file types are rejected and handled safely.
Verify that file batch uploads are secure and do not allow any bypass against the set security measures.

tests.name: Upload of Malicious Files
objectives: Identify the file upload functionality.
Review the project documentation to identify what file types are considered acceptable, and what types would be considered dangerous or malicious.
If documentation is not available then consider what would be appropriate based on the purpose of the application.
Determine how the uploaded files are processed.
Obtain or create a set of malicious files for testing.
Try to upload the malicious files to the application and determine whether it is accepted and processed.

tests.name: Payment Functionality
objectives: Determine whether the business logic for the e-commerce functionality is robust.
Understand how the payment functionality works.
Determine whether the payment functionality is secure.
Determine whether concurrent requests can bypass limits, reuse single-use values or reach states the workflow should not allow.

tests.name: Denial of Inventory
objectives: Identify which actions remove business resources from availability.
Verify eligibility and aggregate allocation limits across reservation states and booking paths.
Demonstrate the effect on another eligible customer and verify recovery.

tests.name: DOM-Based Cross Site Scripting
objectives: Identify DOM sinks.
Build payloads that pertain to every sink type.

tests.name: JavaScript Execution
objectives: Identify sinks and possible JavaScript injection points.

tests.name: HTML Injection
objectives: Identify HTML injection points and assess the severity of the injected content.
Assess what injected markup can do when script execution is blocked, for example by a Content Security Policy.
Determine whether same-origin HTML Injection can undermine CSRF defenses that rely exclusively on HTTP Origin validation.
Assess whether XSS can initiate authenticated state-changing requests without additional interaction after script execution.

tests.name: Client-side URL Redirect
objectives: Identify injection points that handle URLs or paths.
Assess the locations that the system could redirect to.

tests.name: CSS Injection
objectives: Identify CSS injection points.
Assess the impact of the injection.

tests.name: Client-side Resource Manipulation
objectives: Identify sinks with weak input validation.
Assess the impact of the resource manipulation.

tests.name: Cross Origin Resource Sharing
objectives: Identify endpoints that implement CORS.
Ensure that the CORS configuration is secure or harmless.

tests.name: Clickjacking
objectives: Assess application vulnerability to clickjacking attacks.

tests.name: WebSockets
objectives: Identify the usage of WebSockets.
Assess its implementation by using the same tests on normal HTTP channels.
Verify that authentication and authorization are enforced for the handshake and for every subsequent frame, subscription, and pushed event.
Verify that Origin allowlisting uses exact scheme, host, and port comparison.

tests.name: Web Messaging
objectives: Assess the security of the message's origin.
Validate that it's using safe methods and validating its input.

tests.name: Browser Storage
objectives: Determine whether the site is storing sensitive data in client-side storage.
The code handling of the storage objects should be examined for possibilities of injection attacks, such as utilizing unvalidated input or vulnerable libraries.

tests.name: Cross Site Script Inclusion
objectives: Locate sensitive data across the system.
Assess the leakage of sensitive data through various techniques.

tests.name: Reverse Tabnabbing
objectives: Identify links and `window.open()` calls that open a new tab or window without `noopener`.
Assess whether a page opened from the application can change the location of the original page through `window.opener`.

tests.name: Client-side Template Injection
objectives: Identify the client-side framework and its version used by the application.
Detect injection points where user input is reflected into the DOM and processed by the template engine.
Assess if the injection allows for arbitrary JavaScript execution (XSS) via the template syntax.

tests.name: DOM Clobbering
objectives: Identify injection points where user-supplied HTML keeps its `id` or `name` attributes.
Identify scripts that read global variables, `document` properties, or form properties that may be undefined, and pass them to sensitive operations.
Assess whether clobbering those references changes the behavior of the application.

tests.name: Cross-Site Leaks
objectives: Identify responses that change with the authenticated user's state or data.
Determine whether a cross-site page can observe those differences through browser side channels.
Assess whether the application uses the browser defenses that stop cross-site requests or remove the side channels.

tests.name: Client-side Path Traversal
objectives: Identify inputs that reach the path of a client-side request.
Determine which unintended endpoints, methods, and actions those inputs can reach.
Assess the impact, including bypass of anti-CSRF defenses and escalation to Cross Site Scripting.

tests.name: Service Workers
objectives: Identify the service workers an application registers and the scope each one controls.
Determine whether an attacker can influence which script is registered, its scope, or the scripts it loads.
Assess whether the worker's cache and fetch handling can expose or substitute sensitive responses.
Determine whether a worker keeps running after logout or after a vulnerability is fixed.

tests.name: DNS Rebinding
objectives: Identify services in scope that are reachable only from the local machine or an internal network and are used from a browser.
Determine whether those services accept requests with an unexpected `Host` header and without authentication.
Determine whether server-side URL fetching can be redirected to internal addresses by changing DNS answers between validation and use.

tests.name: Server-Sent Events
objectives: Identify the use of Server-Sent Events and how each stream is authenticated.
Determine whether a stream can be read from another origin or by another user.
Verify that authorization is enforced when the stream is opened, for every event it sends, and after the user's access changes.
Assess whether user-controlled data can inject fields or events into the stream, or script into the page that consumes it.

tests.name: API Reconnaissance
objectives: Find all API endpoints supported by the backend server code, documented or undocumented.
Find all parameters for each endpoint supported by the backend server, documented or undocumented.
Discover interesting data related to APIs in HTML and JavaScript sent to clients.

tests.name: API Broken Object Level Authorization
objectives: The objective of this test is to identify whether the API enforces proper **object-level authorization** checks, ensuring that users can only access and manipulate objects they are authorized to interact with.

tests.name: Excessive Data Exposure
objectives: Identify API responses that contain more data than what the client application displays or requires.
Detect sensitive fields returned in API responses such as password hashes, authentication tokens, internal object IDs, PII, or infrastructure details.
Determine whether the API relies on client-side filtering rather than server-side field selection to control data exposure.

tests.name: API Broken Function Level Authorization
objectives: The goal of this test is to determine if the API enforces **role or privilege-based access control** to restrict users from accessing or executing functions they are not authorized to use. This ensures that function-level security boundaries are properly enforced.

tests.name: Testing API Authentication Mechanisms
objectives: Assess whether API keys are scoped, rotated, and transmitted securely.
Determine whether bearer tokens are revocable after logout or credential change.
Verify that OAuth 2.0 token scope is enforced at the authorization server and the resource server.
Evaluate whether APIs that accept session cookies enforce CSRF defenses.
Test whether authentication is enforced for every HTTP method on an endpoint.
Confirm that OAuth token endpoints enforce rate limiting.

tests.name: API Rate Limiting and Resource Consumption
objectives: Verify that per-client and per-endpoint rate limits are enforced.
Identify bypass techniques for existing rate limits.
Confirm that pagination, batch operations, and query complexity are bounded.
Verify that upload size, response size, and timeout controls exist.

tests.name: API Mass Assignment
objectives: Identify API endpoints that accept structured input (JSON, XML, form-encoded) for object creation or modification.
Determine which object properties can be set through client-supplied data by comparing API responses across methods.
Confirm whether privileged or internal-only properties are accepted through REST-specific vectors (PUT vs PATCH, nested JSON, content-type switching).
Test GraphQL mutations for field-level authorization bypass.

tests.name: Inbound Webhooks
objectives: Determine whether inbound webhook endpoints authenticate the sender.
Verify tenant, project, and object binding so a valid event for one customer cannot affect another.
Verify replay and duplicate-delivery handling.
Verify that revoked integrations stop accepting events and remain manageable only by authorized principals.

tests.name: gRPC
objectives: Identify gRPC and gRPC-Web endpoints and recover the service definitions.
Determine whether reflection and built-in services expose information that should not be public.
Assess whether authentication and authorization are enforced for every method, call type, and entry point.
Assess how the service handles unexpected message content, sizes, and errors.

tests.name: GraphQL
objectives: Assess that a secure and production-ready configuration is deployed.
Validate all input fields against generic attacks.
Ensure that proper access controls are applied.

tests.name: WebAssembly Reconnaissance
objectives: Find all WebAssembly modules loaded by the target application, including those not named `.wasm`, compressed, lazy-loaded, loaded through `fetch`, and manual instantiation, or embedded in JavaScript.
Identify the compiler toolchain and source language (e.g., C/C++, Rust, Go, .NET) from section metadata, imports, exports, and glue code.
Detect exposed debugging artifacts: source maps, DWARF information, and the `name` custom section.
Map the infrastructure attack surface by extracting embedded URLs, API endpoints, and internal hostnames or IP addresses.

tests.name: WebAssembly Static Analysis
objectives: Identify the module format and enumerate its sections.
Inspect imports, exports, types, functions, tables, memory, globals, element segments, code, and data.
Convert the binary into readable representations such as WAT, pseudo-code, disassembly, or JavaScript.
Map data-segment offsets and inspect retained debug or compiler metadata in depth.
Use a controlled modification of a test copy to check whether a security-sensitive decision appears to be enforced only in client-side code.

tests.name: WebAssembly Dynamic Analysis
objectives: Intercept the module loading pipeline (`WebAssembly.instantiate`, `WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming`, and `new WebAssembly.Instance`) to capture references to active instances and memory segments.
Capture and log bidirectional function calls, arguments, memory pointers, and return values crossing the JS/Wasm boundary without violating runtime proxy invariants.
Dereference numeric memory pointers to reconstruct strings, structures, and sensitive parameters exchanged between JavaScript and WebAssembly.
Search, inspect, and monitor live linear memory (`WebAssembly.Memory`) for transient secrets, unencrypted credentials, and authorization states using native browser tooling.
Debug executing modules at runtime using instruction-level breakpoints within disassembled WAT views.
Test client-side business logic and validation routines by invoking exported functions with crafted inputs via the browser console.
